activities.caption: call the magnitude — CO's grip on haemoglobin
activities.name: rsCoEstimate

config.prompt: Carbon monoxide binds haemoglobin how many times more strongly than oxygen?
config.why: About 200× — the binding strength that crowds oxygen out of the blood, from a gas with no odour at all.
config.context: The instruments are electrochemical cells, catalytic pellistors and infrared sensors — because the atmosphere that kills is usually the one that changed since yesterday.

activities.anchor: is a sentence that appears in accident reports
activities.caption: bet the current before the arithmetic
activities.name: rsShockPredict

config.q: A hand-to-hand contact through wet skin at household voltage — roughly what current flows through the chest?
config.why: About 240 mA — nearly ten times the fibrillation threshold. Wet skin's hundredfold drop in resistance is what turns ordinary mains voltage lethal; current, path and time set severity.

config.why: Roughly 60% of confined-space fatalities are would-be rescuers, multi-fatality by instinct — the attendant outside does not enter to rescue.

activities.anchor: the design question is always whether the redundancy is
activities.caption: one line of the reliability arithmetic is wrong — find it
activities.name: rsRedundSpot

config.prompt: An engineer sums up system reliability. One line is wrong — click it:
lines: Ten parts in series, each 99.9% reliable
Series multiplies unreliability: 0.999¹⁰ ≈ 99.0% for the whole
So a backup doubles the safety — whatever the numbers say
Common-cause failure — one shared power feed, one firmware bug, one flooded bay — defeats duplication
config.correction: Only independent backups buy the arithmetic — the improvement is multiplicative, not a doubling, and shared modes can collapse the whole stack to single-digit gains.
config.why: Diversity — different suppliers, different physical principles, different failure modes — is priced above copies; the 737 MAX's single-sensor MCAS dependence is the modern case study in hidden common mode.

activities.anchor: Only if the backup fails independently
activities.caption: true or false — what redundancy really buys
activities.name: rsBackupJudge

statements.s: A shared power feed, shared firmware or shared maintenance procedure can collapse a redundant stack to single-digit gains.
statements.why: That is common-cause failure — the reason redundancy engineering is mostly independence analysis.

statements.s: Diversity (different suppliers, different physical principles) is priced above copies.
statements.why: Different failure modes are what independence actually requires.

statements.s: Adding a backup always doubles the safety.
statements.why: Independence is the whole bargain — without it the gain can vanish.

statements.s: The 737 MAX's dependence on a single sensor for MCAS is a case study in hidden common mode.
statements.why: One sensor, one assumption about pilot response — both common causes hiding inside "redundant" intent.

statements.s: Fault-tree analysis works bottom-up, from basic events to the top event.
statements.why: It works top-down — from the top event down to basic events through AND/OR gates; FMEA is the list-first method.
